title: Wszczęcie śledztwa w sprawie pożaru w Skarżysku-Kamiennej
date_evidence: Dateline under the H2 title on the page: "31.08.2026"; body: "celowym wywołaniu w dniu 31 sierpnia 2026 r. pożaru na terenie przedsiębiorstwa WB ELECTRONICS S.A. w Skarżysku-Kamiennej"
key_claim: On 31 August 2026 a prosecutor from the National Prosecutor's Office's organised-crime department in Kraków opened an investigation into participation in foreign-intelligence activity against Poland and a terrorist-type offence, consisting of deliberately starting a fire at WB Electronics S.A. in Skarżysko-Kamienna by planting a device containing flammable materials; warehouse premises were destroyed and the damage is at least 15 million złoty; the case is run jointly with the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and the Kielce regional police, and no charges have yet been brought.
frame_summary: The prosecutor frames the fire from the first day as a foreign-intelligence and terrorist offence carrying a life sentence rather than as an industrial accident, placing the response in the criminal-justice and counter-intelligence system rather than in any industrial-protection regime.
verbatim_quote: W wyniku pożaru zniszczeniu uległy pomieszczenia magazynowe, a wartość wyrządzonej szkody wynosi co najmniej 15 mln zł.
verbatim_list: Śledztwo prowadzone jest w kierunku przestępstwa z art. 130 § 1 i 7 k.k. w zw. z art. 163 § 1 pkt 1 i 3 k.k. zagrożonego karą dożywotniego pozbawienia wolności.
Postępowanie jest prowadzone wspólnie z funkcjonariuszami Agencji Bezpieczeństwa Wewnętrznego oraz Komendy Wojewódzkiej Policji w Kielcach.
Śledztwo jest prowadzone w sprawie. Dotychczas nikomu nie przedstawiono zarzutów.

publisher: European Commission (Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs)
title: Commission issues guidance to strengthen resilience of critical infrastructure
date_evidence: Page header block: "News article / 10 July 2026 / Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs"; footer: "Publication date 10 July 2026"; body: "On 10 July 2026, the European Commission adopted a Communication"
key_claim: On 10 July 2026 the Commission adopted a Communication giving Member States and their critical entities non-binding guidance on technical, security and organisational measures under the Critical Entities Resilience Directive, covering hazards that include drone attacks, hybrid threats and other antagonistic threats, with recommendations on physically protecting critical infrastructure and on employee security management; the guidance is a key action under the EU Action Plan on Drone and Counter-Drone Security.
frame_summary: The Commission presents physical protection against sabotage and drones as a matter for designated critical entities under the CER Directive, to be supported by guidance and national implementation rather than by new EU obligations or money.
verbatim_quote: The Communication offers practical guidance to help address all hazards that could lead to disruptive incidents, including cross-sectoral or cross-border risks, accidents, natural disasters, public health emergencies, drone attacks, hybrid threats and other antagonistic threats.
verbatim_list: On 10 July 2026, the European Commission adopted a Communication providing Member States and their critical entities with non-binding guidance on technical, security and organisational measures to strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure against natural and man-made risks.

It includes recommendations on preventing failures or disruptions of essential services, physically protecting critical infrastructure, mitigating and recovering from disruptive incidents, and improving employee security management and resilience awareness.
The guidance was also identified as a key action under the EU Action Plan on Drone and Counter-Drone Security and includes considerations specifically relevant to countering drone-related threats.

publisher: European Commission (Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs)
title: Critical infrastructure resilience at EU-level (policy page: Directive on the Resilience of Critical Entities)
date_evidence: Evergreen policy page with no dateline; its policy timeline carries entries through 2026 ("2026: Adoption of Commission Guidelines on resilience enhancing measures for critical entities") and the body states "Member States shall identify critical entities by 17 July 2026". Accessed 16/09/2026.
key_claim: The CER Directive covers eleven sectors (energy; transport; banking; financial market infrastructure; health; drinking water; wastewater; digital infrastructure; public administration; space; production, processing and distribution of food), and Member States were required to identify critical entities by 17 July 2026 on the basis of national risk assessments due by 17 January 2026; defence manufacturing is not among the listed sectors.
frame_summary: The Commission frames critical-entity resilience as a sector-list regime built on essential services to society and the economy, with the eleven sectors fixed by the Directive and the identification of entities left to Member States.
verbatim_quote: Taking into account the outcomes of the risk assessment, Member States shall identify critical entities by 17 July 2026.
verbatim_list: The Directive covers eleven sectors:
Energy;
Transport;
Banking;
Financial market infrastructure;
Health;
Drinking water;
Wastewater;
Digital infrastructure;
Public administration;
Space;
Production, processing and distribution of food.
Pursuant to the CER Directive, Member States shall adopt a national strategy for enhancing the resilience of critical entities and carry out a risk assessment by 17 January 2026.
notes: Evergreen reference page used for the sector list only; rendered in the bibliography as accessed 16/09/2026. title: Russia is trying to bully Europe into abandoning Ukraine (Maksym Beznosiuk and Will Dixon)
key_claim: In late August and early September 2026 Germany blamed Russia for the failed August drone attack on Leipzig Airport, Slovak authorities foiled an attempted arson attack on a Ukrainian drone manufacturer, Estonian investigators were probing possible Russian involvement in a fire at premises used by a supplier of unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine, and Poland's prime minister said Russia was likely behind the blaze at a Polish weapons factory; the authors judge that Russia's escalation is calibrated to stay below the threshold that would trigger a military response.
frame_summary: The authors argue that the sabotage wave is a coercion campaign by a weakening Russia aimed at frightening European publics out of supporting Ukraine, and that Europe should expect more grey-zone attacks on infrastructure rather than a direct military confrontation.
verbatim_quote: For now, Russia’s escalation appears calibrated to remain below the threshold that could trigger a military response.
verbatim_list: In Slovakia, authorities foiled an attempted arson attack against a Ukrainian drone manufacturer.
Estonian investigators are probing possible Russian involvement in a fire at premises used by a company supplying unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Russia was likely behind a blaze at a Polish factory supplying weapons to Ukraine, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said this week.

Instead, Europe should prepare to face mounting grey zone aggression including air space incursions, attacks on infrastructure, and other acts of sabotage as Putin attempts to intimidate Europe and deprive Ukraine of vital support.

title: Europe’s Defense Factories: More Urgency Please (Miro Sedlák, Europe's Edge)
key_claim: The European Defence Industry Programme work programme adopted on 30 March 2026 contains a line item nobody expected: in the first call for energetic components it offers recipients up to €500,000 per project to physically protect production sites, and the author reads this as a real expectation that the factories Brussels is subsidising will be targets.
frame_summary: The author argues that EDIP has the right architecture but that money is no longer the constraint, production capacity and political will are, and that the site-protection line item shows Brussels already expects its subsidised factories to be attacked.
verbatim_quote: Page 10 of the work program, in the first call for energetic components, offers recipients up to €500,000 per project to physically protect production sites.
verbatim_list: The line item for drone protection in the work program was not a metaphor. It describes a real expectation that the factories Brussels is now subsidizing will, in their lifetime, be targets in a war Europe is not yet organized to fight.

Factories built to produce counter-drone weapons can now claim EU money to protect themselves from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The Commission adopted the work program on 30 March, but the policy consequences will be harder to agree on.
notes: Structural anchor in the 3-6 month band (published 23 April 2026, 146 days before scan date): the canonical account of the EDIP site-protection line item that gives the signal its funding baseline. title: Ochrona zbrojeniówki do poprawy? "Płot jak w ogródkach działkowych" (Bartłomiej Chudy)
key_claim: Deputy interior minister Czesław Mroczek said the WB Electronics site's CCTV recorded a masked intruder, that the ministry would draw up recommendations because protection plans at key defence plants must be richer than at this plant, and that police checks and presence at such sites had already been increased; defence24 deputy editor Mariusz Marszałkowski said the plant's fence was at allotment-garden level and that the duty to arrange site protection lies with the firms themselves, the state supporting them through clear regulation, while counter-drone systems cannot be used in Poland in peacetime.
frame_summary: The piece frames plant security as primarily the company's duty, with the state's role limited to counter-intelligence, police presence, recommendations and clearer regulation, and treats further sabotage attempts on Polish defence plants as a matter of time.
verbatim_quote: Po stronie samych firm jest obowiązek przygotowania ochrony obiektu, a państwo może je wspierać np. poprzez przejrzyste regulacje. Z drugiej strony nie można w Polsce użyć systemu antydronowego, gdyż jest to zabronione w czasach pokoju.

title: PET: Rusland forbereder sabotage mod dansk forsvarsindustri
date_evidence: Visible byline above the headline: "Ritzau 02.09.26 Kl. 22:08" (dd.mm.yy, i.e. 2 September 2026); og:image path carries "/scanpix/2026-09/"
key_claim: Emil Græsholm, head of counter-intelligence at Denmark's PET, said on 2 September 2026 that Russian intelligence services are actively preparing sabotage against the Danish defence industry, naming arson as a possible method and firms tied to military aid to Ukraine as the main targets; Russia has tried to recruit ordinary Danes to report on access and security conditions around factories, and the counter-intelligence chief urged defence-industry firms to raise their security.
frame_summary: PET frames the threat as concrete enough to warrant a public warning and puts the immediate remedy on the firms, which are asked to raise their own security, with the service's role being detection and warning.

verbatim_list: Opgaverne kan for eksempel lyde på at undersøge og oplyse adgangs- og sikkerhedsforhold omkring en fabrik eller virksomhed i Danmark.
Han nævner specifikt brandstiftelse som et muligt mål fra russisk side.
Blandt målene er særligt virksomheder i forsvarsindustrien med tilknytning til militær hjælp til Ukraine, lyder det.

title: Emco: Blast at ammo depot in Bulgaria was sabotage, state is failing to do its job
key_claim: After explosions on the night of 11 September 2026 at an Emco ammunition depot near Gorni Varpishta, the company said the blast was sabotage, that the warehouse had been unused for months and had passed seven interior-ministry inspections since the start of the year, and that none of the investigations into more than 10 similar incidents across the industry had been concluded; interior minister Ivan Demerdzhiev said there was neglect of storage conditions and of the method of security, that every warehouse in the country would be inspected, and that since the owners cannot take measures the state will step in.
frame_summary: The piece sets the manufacturer's frame (state incompetence in the face of repeated sabotage) against the interior minister's (owner neglect of storage and security, with the state now stepping in to inspect and instruct), presenting the dispute over who is responsible for guarding arms depots as unresolved.
verbatim_quote: “Since the owners cannot take measures, the state will step in and do what is necessary. We see a lot of shortcomings, not only in this enterprise,” he said.
verbatim_list: Emco said that the warehouse has been subject to periodic inspections by the Ministry of Interior authorities, seven times since the beginning of the year, the most recent one being 20 days ago.
None of the investigations into more than 10 similar incidents across all leading companies in the industry have been concluded, the company said.
“There is a neglect of the conditions under which explosives and ammunition are stored. There is also a neglect of the method of security.”
“We do not rule out external interference, but when you have neglected the conditions under which explosives are stored and security, then one does not exclude the other,” Demerdzhiev said.
notes: English-language Bulgarian news site carrying both the company statement and the interior minister's remarks; the counter-argument draws on the minister's neglect framing.
